account:
It is day 1, just before eight, and I am at the town hall for my morning office hours. I read and returned both appointment books. Today I must inspect grain at the mill at ten, lunch at home at noon, deal with council letters at thirteen, take tea with the neighbour at fifteen, return to the office at sixteen-thirty, and meet the innkeeper in the great hall at eighteen sharp. He confirmed that I need prepare nothing.

There have been several small, possibly connected oddities. The neighbour relayed an unconfirmed report from Townsfolk 02 about lights or decorations at the bakery; the baker reportedly knew of no special occasion. The secretary heard that the baker carried a sack of bread near the plaza. I myself saw Freight carrying a bread sack near the town hall yesterday evening. Freight was seeking the miller and builder to coordinate warehouse supplies, and I heard the innkeeper invite the builder to a private supplies discussion at the inn. This morning I heard the innkeeper speaking and shouting, but could not understand the words; he is now outside near the hall.

These observations suggest some coordination of bread, supplies, and perhaps preparations for a gathering, involving the innkeeper, builder, Freight, and possibly the miller and baker. A celebration is a possibility, not something I know. Ordinary business could explain much of it, and no danger or damage has been reported. The innkeeper's insistence on an eighteen-sharp meeting in the great hall may be related, but I do not yet know that. Separately, the town accounts were not found on any of the four great hall tables yesterday; I have no evidence connecting that problem to the supplies activity. I should keep my appointments and ask straightforward questions rather than treat rumours as established facts.
